newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Manuel clarifies forex control remarks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Manuel clarifies forex control remarks.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel on Tuesday reaffirmed his commitment to the abolition of foreign exchange controls, but said he would consider prudential requirements for the savings industry.
Clarifying remarks at a news briefing earlier, Manuel said through a spokeswoman that South Africa had to examine options exercised by other countries in capital account liberalisation.
"The Finance Minister remains committed to the gradual lifting of exchange controls," the spokeswoman said.

Manuel had said at the news briefing that South Africa had not decided finally whether to go the route of Mexico and abolish all foreign exchange controls or whether, like Chile, to retain some controls.
He cited the example of France, which imposed limits of companies investing abroad.
"What the end product is at this stage is still up in the air. Will we retain a modicum of control as in Chile or would you go the Mexican route has not finally been settled," he said.
Manuel's remarks appeared to contradict his own macro-economic strategy, which states: "...all remaining exchange controls will be dismantled as soon as circumstances are favourable."

But his spokeswoman said he was referring only to the possibility of a prudential requirement for institutions, such as the 10 percent limit on the foreign investment of savings applied by many countries.
"This is not generally regarded as a foreign exchange control," she said.
The spokeswoman quoted Department of Finance Director General Maria Ramos as saying capital account liberalisation had to be managed responsibly.

"We have to lift exchange controls with institutional supports in place in order to maintain the integrity of the financial system...there has to be responsible management of the country's savings," Ramos said.
